Before I make my final decision on process-water allocation, I'd like to hear updates from quality, maintenance, and EHS. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I have a lab test completed this morning that hasn't been uploaded to the shared quality folder yet. The reclaimed-water conductivity came in at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, so reclaimed water would exceed that limit. Line Y's process limit is 2,200, so reclaimed water is within spec for Line Y. However, Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, and the reclaimed water is only acceptable for that batch after a conductivity test is recorded — which is what I'm doing now.

transcript.text: I need to share an important maintenance finding. My inspection of the recovery skid — documented in my notebook but not yet in the work-order system — found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use, and after that flush it can deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour. This is critical for planning: at 600 liters per hour, delivering the full 2,400 liters would take 4 hours of run time, plus the 3-hour flush upfront before any reclaimed water is available.

That review found that reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million, and that each use day requires a signed sanitizer log. decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Allocate reclaimed water to Line Y only. Line X cannot use reclaimed water due to conductivity exceeding its process limit. Line Y's batch requires 1,800 liters, which is within the available 2,400 liters. Before delivery, the recovery skid must undergo a 3-hour membrane flush, sanitizer must be adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm with a signed sanitizer log for each use day, and Ravi must complete recording the conductivity test. After the flush, reclaimed water will be delivered at 600 liters per hour, requiring 3 hours to deliver the 1,800 liters for Line Y's batch. The remaining 600 liters of reclaimed water will be held in reserve.

commitments.detail: Complete uploading the conductivity test result to the shared quality folder before reclaimed water is released to Line Y.
Perform the 3-hour membrane flush on the recovery skid before any reclaimed water is delivered, and document in the work-order system.
Verify and adjust sanitizer level to exactly 0.3 ppm and ensure a signed sanitizer log is completed for each day of reclaimed water use during the restriction.
Sign the water-control plan authorizing 1,800 liters of reclaimed water to Line Y only, with 600 liters held in reserve.
